issues.t: Automatic transmission harsh shifts or failure
issues.sym: The O/D (overdrive) light flashes, shifts are harsh or late, the car drops into a lower gear on its own, or it loses power and slips. Some owners report repeated failures and rebuilds.
issues.why: Automatic Probes use Ford's CD4E transaxle, which has a reputation for internal wear. Ford issued several bulletins for harsh shifts and engagement tied to trouble codes 628 and P0741 (torque converter clutch slipping). A flashing O/D light means the transmission computer has stored a fault.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read and check the fluid level and condition. If it is slipping, avoid hard driving. On a car this age a used or rebuilt transmission is usually the most sensible fix.

issues.t: Engine stalls or shuts off while driving
issues.sym: The engine dies without warning while driving, sometimes with the check engine light or all dash lights coming on. Power steering and brake assist get much harder until it restarts.
issues.why: Owners have filed many stalling complaints with NHTSA, including some that led to crashes. Ford released an engine computer reprogramming for stalling, and failed crankshaft and camshaft position sensors are another known cause.
issues.next: Treat stalling as a safety problem. Have the codes read and ask whether the stalling reflash was ever done. Have the crank and cam sensors tested.

issues.t: Intermittent no-start, cranks but won't fire
issues.sym: The engine cranks normally but will not start, then starts fine another time. It may also cut out and stall once running.
issues.why: Owners and technicians point to the ignition system: the distributor (with its built-in pickup and ignition parts), engine grounds and position sensors. These faults are often heat-related and come and go.
issues.next: Have a shop check for spark and fuel pressure while the problem is happening. The distributor is a common fix; also have the main engine ground wires cleaned.

issues.t: Hard to start when cold or after sitting
issues.sym: Long cranking before the engine catches, especially on a cold morning or after the car has sat for a while. Once running it is usually fine.
issues.why: This is the most-reported 1997 Probe problem. Ford issued a bulletin for hard starting caused by fuel pressure bleeding off while the car sits (fuel pressure leak-down), which leaves the injectors without enough pressure at the next start.
issues.next: Have a shop do a fuel pressure and leak-down test. A leaking injector, fuel pressure regulator or pump check valve is the usual culprit.

issues.t: Timing belt tensioner spring can break (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning. The engine can suddenly stall while driving, leaving you without power steering.
issues.why: On some 1997 Probes a spring in the timing belt tensioner could break and get caught in the belt. Ford recalled about 5,700 cars in 1998 (NHTSA 98V206, Ford 98S30) to inspect and fix the tensioner.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls with Ford. If you are unsure whether it was done, have the timing belt and tensioner inspected.

issues.t: Timing belt wears out and snaps
issues.sym: The engine suddenly quits while driving and cranks over fast but will not start again.
issues.why: Both Probe engines use a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule. Many neglected Probes simply broke their belts. Owners say these engines are non-interference, so a snapped belt usually does not bend valves.
issues.next: If you do not know when the belt was last changed, replace the belt and tensioner now. If it has already snapped, have the belt replaced and the engine checked before assuming the worst.

issues.t: Check engine light with code P1794 (V6)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on and code P1794 is stored, usually with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletin 96245 for 1997 Probes with the 2.5L V6 that turn on the check engine light and store code P1794. The code relates to the power supply signal the engine computer sees, so it is often electrical rather than mechanical.
issues.next: Have the code read and the battery, terminals and engine computer power connections checked, and ask a shop to look up Ford bulletin 96245 if the light keeps coming back.

issues.t: Rough running and hesitation from a failing sensor
issues.sym: The engine runs rough, hesitates or skips when you accelerate or shift, idles poorly or loses power.
issues.why: This is the most commonly reported Probe engine complaint on RepairPal. Failing throttle position sensors, mass air flow sensors and crank or cam position sensors are frequent causes. Ford issued a service tip to replace the mass air flow sensor as a full assembly.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the sensor readings checked with a scan tool before replacing parts. Also check plugs and plug wires.

issues.t: Power steering belt snaps or steering rack fails
issues.sym: Steering suddenly gets very heavy, a squeal or buzz from the pump, fluid leaks, or a clicking noise when turning.
issues.why: Owners report power steering belts breaking at highway speed, leaking or failed rack-and-pinion units, and noisy pumps.
issues.next: Check the belt and power steering fluid regularly. If you find a leak or the steering gets heavy, have the belt, pump, hoses and rack inspected.

issues.sym: The airbag warning light flashes or stays on.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin noting that a poor connection at the clock spring (the coiled wiring behind the steering wheel that feeds the driver airbag) can cause this.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. While the light is on the airbags may not work, so do not put this off.

issues.sym: A front seat belt rolls back slowly or hangs loose instead of retracting fully.
issues.why: Ford found the belt webbing can get twisted behind the B-pillar trim, which slows retraction. Owners also report worn retractors.
issues.next: Have the trim removed and the webbing straightened. If the belt still does not retract or lock, replace the retractor.

issues.t: Clutch pedal sticks partway to the floor
issues.sym: On manual cars the clutch pedal stays down or sticks halfway, making it hard or impossible to shift.
issues.why: This is a reported Probe problem around 100,000 miles. A leaking clutch master or slave cylinder lets hydraulic pressure drop so the pedal does not return.
issues.next: Check the clutch fluid reservoir for low or dirty fluid and look for leaks. Replacing the clutch master and/or slave cylinder and bleeding the system usually fixes it.

issues.t: Oil leaking into the spark plug wells
issues.sym: Oil smell, oil on the spark plugs or plug wires, and misfires or rough running.
issues.why: Owners report engine oil seeping into the spark plug wells, which usually comes from a hardened valve cover gasket or plug tube seals.
issues.next: Replace the valve cover gasket and seals and clean the plug wells. Replace any oil-soaked plug wires.

issues.t: Won't start with the fuel cutoff light on
issues.sym: The engine will not start or dies, and a fuel cutoff warning stays on.
issues.why: The Probe has a fuel cutoff (inertia) switch that shuts off the fuel pump after a jolt such as a pothole or minor impact. If it trips or the switch fails, the pump gets no power.
issues.next: Check the owner's manual for the reset button location and press it. If the light keeps coming on, have the switch and its wiring checked.

issues.t: Ticking engine noise and low oil pressure
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping noise from the engine, rough running, stalling or reduced power, sometimes with the oil light.
issues.why: RepairPal lists a defective oil pump as a cause of these symptoms on the Probe. Low oil pressure starves the hydraulic valve lifters, which then tick.
issues.next: Check the oil level first and stop driving if the oil light is on. Have the oil pressure tested before replacing parts.

issues.t: Shifter stuck in Park from a bad brake light switch
issues.sym: On automatic cars the shifter will not move out of Park even with the brake pressed, and the brake lights may not work.
issues.why: The shift lock only releases when the brake light switch tells it you are braking. Ford bulletins note a faulty brake lamp switch can disable the shift interlock.
issues.next: Check whether the brake lights work. Use the shift lock override if needed, and have the brake light switch replaced.

issues.sym: The outside door handle goes loose or stops opening the door.
issues.why: Owners report broken door handles and a broken return spring inside the outside handle.
issues.next: Replace the handle or its spring. The door panel has to come off to reach it.

issues.sym: The power antenna will not go up or down, or the radio has poor reception.
issues.why: Owners note the power antenna on these cars rarely works anymore. The mast and motor gears wear and jam.
issues.next: Replace the antenna mast or the whole motor assembly, or fit a fixed antenna.

issues.t: Airbag warning label missing child seat caution (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you would notice while driving.
issues.why: On some 1996 Probes the sun visor airbag caution label left out the warning about rear-facing child seats in the front passenger seat. Ford recalled the cars (NHTSA 96V090) and mailed owners a new label.
issues.next: Never put a rear-facing child seat in front of an airbag. If your visor label lacks this warning, Ford can supply the correct one.
